pl-l3d1prae-d1e114.summary: Opens the treatment of the incarnation with Gal 4:4–5: when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the Law, to redeem those under the Law so that we might receive adoption as sons.
claims: God sent his Son in the fullness of time to redeem those under the Law.

pl-l3d1prae-d1e120.summary: Explains the fullness of time as the time of grace beginning with the Savior's advent, the time of mercy, in which grace and truth came through Christ: grace because what the Law commanded is fulfilled through charity, truth because the ancient promise of redemption is fulfilled. The Son's mission is the incarnation itself, since he was sent by appearing visibly in human form, a point treated sufficiently in Book 1.
claims: The fullness of time is the time of grace.
The Son's mission is the incarnation, his visible appearance in human form.

pl-l3d1prae.summary: Opens Book 3 with Gal 4:4: in the fullness of time God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the Law, to redeem those under the Law. The fullness of time is the time of grace, beginning with the Savior's coming, in which grace (the Law's precepts fulfilled through charity) and truth (the ancient promise of redemption fulfilled) come through Christ. The Son's mission is the incarnation itself, his visible appearance in human form, as treated earlier.
claims: The fullness of time is the time of grace begun with Christ's coming.
The Son's mission is the incarnation.
